title: repository_test: content_hash bytea/uuid type mismatch and untyped SQL parameters (11 blocks)
symptom: 11 test blocks in tests/integration/repository_test.zig fail. Representative errors: C42804 column "content_hash" is of type bytea but expression is of type uuid; C42P18 could not determine data type of parameter $1; and TC-REPO-02-01 failing at repository_test.zig:180 on `try std.testing.expect(schema.rows.len == 1)`.
root_cause_analysis: The fixtures insert a generated UUID into repository_artifacts.content_hash, which the migration defines as bytea, so PostgreSQL rejects the assignment outright (C42804). Separately, several queries pass bare $N placeholders in positions where PostgreSQL cannot infer a type, producing C42P18 at parse time, which is the ISS-0120 pattern. TC-REPO-02-01 information_schema probe also returns 0 rows, consistent with the public/tenant_default schema-qualification issue tracked separately as ISS-0185.
impact: 11 of the 86 remaining failures in test-integration-svc. Repository artifact immutability (REPO-02) has no passing evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures write a bytea value (for example the digest of the artifact bytes) to content_hash, not a UUID
Every placeholder in repository_test.zig carries an explicit type cast where the context is ambiguous; tools/lint_sql_param_types.py stays at 0 BLOCKER/MAJOR
TC-REPO-02-01 schema probe is qualified to the schema the table actually lives in
zig build test-integration-svc shows 0 failures attributed to repository_test.zig
related: ISS-0150 / GH #482 - the run that surfaced this
notes: Filed per CLAUDE.md 'No Issue Left Local-Only' and the 'filed and forwarded, not fixed here' scope boundary. ISS-0150 fixed 3 root causes (33 blocks) with zero regressions; this cluster has a distinct root cause and belongs in its own run.

resolution.summary: Re-verified against a freshly-migrated bpm_test rather than trusting the original filing: the original filing's TC-REPO-02-01 description (0 rows) did not match current reality (2 rows -- an FK-protected tenant_default.repository_artifacts shadow that GBL-138's reconciliation had missed, since it only copied GBL-134's shadow list and not GBL-136's separate follow-up list). Root-caused and fixed via a new forward-fix migration (GBL-139) plus schema-qualifying the probe. The content_hash bytea/uuid mismatch (7 sites, all in artifact_versions inserts) and the untyped-parameter issue (1 genuine off-by-one $2 reference) were both real and independent of the schema issue, as predicted. Fixing content_hash surfaced 3 more previously-masked bugs in the same file (stale table/column names post-rename, a missing RETURNING clause) that had never been reached because the content_hash error aborted each transaction before those statements ran.
resolution.resolution_strategy: 1) migrations/GBL-139_iss0183_reconcile_gbl136_tenant_default_reprovision.sql -- idempotent forward-fix re-applying GBL-136's exact 8-table RESTRICT-only drop logic (GBL-134/135/136/137/138 are immutable per established convention). 2) tests/integration/repository_test.zig: schema-qualified TC-REPO-02-01's information_schema probe to table_schema='public'; replaced all 7 gen_random_uuid()-for-content_hash sites with digest(<unique-per-row-string>, 'sha256') via a dedicated extra placeholder (reusing $1 with an added ::text cast throws C42P08, since $1 was already inferred as uuid elsewhere in the same statement); fixed TC-REPO-04-01's $2-with-one-bound-param off-by-one to $1; fixed TC-REPO-06-01's event_type_name column (real name: `name`) and its '1.0' text literal for the INTEGER schema_version column; renamed all form_schema_registry references to repository_form_schemas (migration 072 renamed the table months ago); added RETURNING version_id to TC-REPO-11-02's INSERT...SELECT so its rows.len assertion is meaningful. 3) Added a dedicated `test-integration-repository` build.zig step (matching the existing ENV-01/ISS-107 pattern) for isolated re-verification.

resolution.prevention: The dual-schema-shadow class of bug (anti-patterns.md) needs its reconciliation migrations (GBL-138-style) to enumerate ALL prior GBL-13x shadow-drop migrations' table lists, not just the most recent/largest one -- a follow-up migration's own follow-up list is easy to miss when reconciling after a reprovisioning event. Consider a shared source-of-truth table-name array (or a lint check comparing GBL-13x DROP lists against each other) rather than copy-pasting subsets across files.
